chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Losing his eyesight
summary: He recalls losing the right eye in Portland, Oregon, the specialists he consulted, and the Johns Hopkins doctor who said he would never see again.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That was in 1968, were you having problems with your eyes then.

No, I was all right then. It was in '70 when -- let me see, the band was at the Radio City up in the Rainbow Room, Rainbow Grill and I was getting ready to -- I was just going to the grill and I picked up some music and it looked like it was fading away. I said, man, I'm losing my eyesight. Sure enough, I lost my right eye when I was out there in Portland, Oregon.
What were you doing out in Portland.
I was with Duke. We was out there and I used to drink a whole lot of liquor you know. I.W. Harper.
We spent a few days together. And enjoyed every minute of it.

So I came back to New York and I went down to this eye specialist on 45th Street and she says, I don't know what she said. Anyway, she give me a note to the doctor and I give it to him and -- she said you got a good left eye and it will last you all your life.
It's a retina in this left eye that went out and in the right eye too, both went.
Did the doctors ever say whether they could replace it.

No, I went down to Johns Hopkins Hospital and to one of the greatest eye doctors they said in the world, I went down to him and I had to wait three months to see him, because he was in Japan and when he came back I went down and saw him and he said stop spending your money, stop going around to these doctors. They can't do nothing for you. You'll never see again.
